expected: Request browser notification permission, register the service worker, subscribe to push, register the subscription with the backend

states_handled.error: silent (console.warn in DEV only, no toast)

code_findings: CRITICAL/systemic: this manual, gated flow duplicates an UNGATED automatic one in context/AuthContext.jsx:13-32 (registerWebPush), which runs on every successful login and every session restore with a valid token, calling reg.pushManager.subscribe({userVisibleOnly:true, ...}) without checking Notification.permission first. That call itself triggers the native browser permission prompt - meaning users can see the OS/browser push-permission dialog on app load, bypassing this banner's intended opt-in UX entirely.

CRITICAL/cross-account bug: AuthContext.jsx:20-28 only calls webSubscribe() when `!sub` (no existing browser-level PushSubscription). On a shared device, if user A subscribes then logs out and user B logs in, reg.pushManager.getSubscription() still returns A's subscription, so `sub` is truthy and webSubscribe is skipped for B - B's account is never registered for push, while the PushToken row server-side (app/notifications/router.py:52-75, keyed by whichever user last called web-subscribe) remains associated with A. `DELETE /notifications/web-unsubscribe` exists specifically to prevent this (comment: 'called when user denies permission or logs out') but per dependency-map.md and AuthContext/SettingsPage, it is never called anywhere in the web app - logout() (AuthContext.jsx:59-62) does not unsubscribe.

Reloading the page, or the focus-triggered re-fetch (line 129-131), will show the notification as unread again, since getNotifications() re-fetches server truth which was never updated for that single item.
